positions.title: Teaching Assistant
positions.description: Taught Introduction to Computing for Data Analytics, a course focused on providing students in the statistics department at CMU with the programming background necessary to progress through their other courses. The course was taught entirely in R and was geared towards Freshmen and Sophomores. As a TA I helped write and grade assignments, helped decide the overall structure of the course, and taught recitations weekly.

positions.title: Data Analyst
positions.description: I worked as a fully-fledged member of the data analytics team where I developed business intelligence tools both for internal usage as well as for sale as a product to external clients. Internally, I developed a series of metrics and visualizations for analyzing employee performance which is now widely in use by the project management team as well as creating replicators to add new sources of data for other teams to use in their work. I also developed a tool called Vision for tax collectors to analyze the workflow of their tax collection centers and identify blockages. I was part of the team rolling out this product which has already generated approximately $225,000 dollars in annual revenue.

positions.title: Intern
positions.description: During my time at the SEI, I acted as the lead intern for a team of approximately 4 interns working on a wide range of projects from designing physical network space to conducting cyber security education research. I also spent time constructing labs for a graduate level cyber security course for penetration testing before transitioning into a more traditional sysadmin role as my course load at CMU increased.

company.name: Software Engineering Institute | Carnegie Mellon University

positions.title: Intern
positions.description: I worked as an intern for the Mobile Edge Computing team revolutionizing how mobile networks work. I had three main projects during my time there. I created new tools for use in testing network performance in a distributed network environment. I also improved upon core infrastructure libraries to facilitate the work of my coworkers. Finally, I helped redesign and re-implement portions of the PKI interface and then developed the REST API for use with said interface alongside SDK examples for demonstration of said API.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence Representation and Problem Solving

organizations.name: Alpha Tau Omega
organizations.description: As the social service chair for my fraternity, I network with various charities and organizations both on campus in CMU as well as in the greater Pittsburgh area to organize volunteering events for the members of my organization in order to broaden their perspective of our world as a whole. These activities range from things like cleaning up illegal dumping sites to volunteering at food banks and working on community farms. I also either arrange for speakers from said organizations or lead the debriefs myself to make sure that the participants understand the importance of their work.

organizations.name: Student Dormitory Council
organizations.description: As booth chair, I lead the design and construction of an exhibit contained within a wooden building of our construction to be put on display for the local Pittsburgh community in the Spring. My responsibilities as booth chair are very wide ranged including things like leading creative brainstorming sessions and leading the programmers/electrical engineers in the construction of games to be put in the booth. The overall summary of my role is I design and implement the user experience for our booth while also handling the various logistical challenges associated with constructing a booth.
